statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, r is the unique binary tree T described by descriptions. Equivalently: the set of node labels of r is exactly V, with each v in V labeling exactly one node; the root of r is labeled root; for every i, if descriptions[i][2] = 1 then the node labeled descriptions[i][0] in r has as its immediate left child the node labeled descriptions[i][1], and if descriptions[i][2] = 0 then it has as its immediate right child the node labeled descriptions[i][1]; and for every v in V, if no row has parent v and isLeft 1 then the left child slot of the node labeled v is Tree.Null, and if no row has parent v and isLeft 0 then its right child slot is Tree.Null. Here immediate child means the root of the corresponding left or right subtree (Tree.Null if that subtree is Tree.Null).
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values (each value is a distinct node, every non-root value has exactly one parent, each parent has at most one left and at most one right child, and the parent-child graph is acyclic and connected with the unique parentless value as root). Let V be the set of all integers appearing in any row of descriptions (as descriptions[i][0] or descriptions[i][1]), and let root be the unique value in V that never occurs as descriptions[i][1].

statement: For every descriptions satisfying the precondition, create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, arithmetic overflow, or out-of-bounds access).
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, the multiset of node labels of r is exactly V: every v in V labels exactly one node of r, and no node of r has a label outside V.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values. Let V be the set of all integers appearing in any row of descriptions (as descriptions[i][0] or descriptions[i][1]).

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, r is not Tree.Null and the label of the root of r is root, the unique value in V that does not occur as descriptions[i][1] for any i.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values. Let V be the set of all integers appearing in any row of descriptions, and let root be the unique value in V that does not occur as descriptions[i][1] for any i.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(descriptions), in r the node labeled descriptions[i][0] has the node labeled descriptions[i][1] as its immediate left child when descriptions[i][2] = 1, and as its immediate right child when descriptions[i][2] = 0.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, every immediate child edge in r comes from a row of descriptions: for every node v in r, if its immediate left child is a node u then there is an i with descriptions[i][0] = v, descriptions[i][1] = u, and descriptions[i][2] = 1; and if its immediate right child is a node u then there is an i with descriptions[i][0] = v, descriptions[i][1] = u, and descriptions[i][2] = 0.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, for every v in V, the node labeled v in r is a leaf (both its immediate left and right children are Tree.Null) if and only if v does not occur as descriptions[i][0] for any i.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values. Let V be the set of all integers appearing in any row of descriptions.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r and create_binary_tree(d') returns a result r', we have r = r' (structural equality of Tree).
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values. Let d' be any permutation of the rows of descriptions (the same multiset of rows in a different order); by the validity guarantee d' also satisfies the validity precondition.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, for every row i let c = descriptions[i][1]. The set of node labels in the subtree of r rooted at the node labeled c is exactly the set of all v in V such that v = c or there is a directed path from c to v in the graph whose edges are the parent-to-child pairs given by the rows (ignoring the isLeft labels).
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values. Let V be the set of all integers appearing in any row of descriptions.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, for every v in V, the depth of the node labeled v in r (the number of edges on the path from the root of r to that node) equals the length of the unique directed path from root to v in the graph whose edges are the parent-to-child pairs given by the rows.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values. Let V be the set of all integers appearing in any row of descriptions, and let root be the unique value in V that does not occur as descriptions[i][1] for any i.

statement: Whenever create_binary_tree(descriptions) returns a result r, for every i, the immediate parent in r of the node labeled descriptions[i][1] is the node labeled descriptions[i][0]; equivalently, every value that occurs as a child in descriptions has exactly that listed value as its parent in r.
preconditions: descriptions satisfies the problem constraints and validity guarantee: 1 <= len(descriptions) <= 10^4; every descriptions[i] has length 3; for each row [p,c,l], 1 <= p,c <= 10^5 and l in {0,1}; and the rows describe a valid binary tree of unique values.
